title: When can you change your golf ball?
question: On which occasions are you allowed to replace your ball with another one while playing a hole?

choices.text: If you can't find your original ball after searching
When taking relief under the Rules (such as from a penalty area or abnormal course condition)
If your ball only has a small scratch
If your ball has a significant cut or crack
Any time you feel like it, even during play of a hole

explanation: You may substitute a new ball if your original is lost, when taking relief under the rules, or if it's severely damaged (like a big cut or crack). A minor scratch isn't enough, and you can't just switch at any moment.

juniorVersion.title: When are you allowed to swap your golf ball for a new one?
juniorVersion.question: While you are playing a hole, when can you change your ball for a different one?

choices.text: If you cannot find your ball after looking for it
When you take a drop because of the rules (like dropping out of a puddle or long grass area)
If your ball just has a little scratch
If your ball has a big cut or crack in it
Any time you want, even during the hole

juniorVersion.explanation: You can change your ball if you cannot find it, if you are taking a drop because of a rule, or if your ball has a big cut or crack. You cannot switch your ball just because it has a small scratch or whenever you want.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Dropping a ball from knee height to play after moving it for a rule reason.
Getting to move your ball without penalty because of something like water or a rule problem.
A big mark or break in your golf ball that can change how it rolls.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Ask children if they have ever found a damaged or lost ball, and discuss when it's fair to use a new one.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking you can always swap your ball for a new one for any reason.
Not realising a small scratch does not let you change your ball.
